item1_EA_OR_2.99_pvalue.finding: OR=2.99 arises in TWO different cells of gwas_p11_mapping_sensitivity.csv: original MAPPED_GENE convention (OR=2.9872) and author-REPORTED convention (OR=2.9905). They are different 2x2 tables, so the identical 3-s.f. OR is coincidence, not a copy error in the table.
item1_EA_OR_2.99_pvalue.verdict: Both p-values are correct for their own 2x2: MAPPED p_one_sided=8.68e-16 (two-sided 1.02e-15, matches S5 RD x EA); author-reported p=0.01506 (one-sided and two-sided coincide here: no more-extreme table exists in the other tail). If the manuscript pairs author-reported OR=2.99 with p=8.7e-16 that association is wrong; the author-reported cell (n=45 genes, k=7) is only nominally significant.

item2_MDD_GDstrict_LOO_q.verdict: Text "0.11-0.15" matches NEITHER family exactly. 36-family LOO range = 0.107-0.111; 48-family LOO range = 0.143-0.148; including the joint LOO-brain-tau variant (48-family) the range is 0.081-0.148. popgen read 0.1426/0.1478/0.0811 = the 48-family xlsx S5 values, correct. Recommend (48-family convention): "q = 0.14-0.15 for the single-component LOO variants (0.081 for the joint LOO-brain-tau variant)"; under the 36-family convention "q = 0.107-0.111".

item3_trait_set_sizes.verdict: Minimum trait set = Crohn disease (95 universe genes), not 103. 103 is k_overlap of RD x Educational attainment (see S5), i.e. an overlap count, not a trait-set size. Correct text: "trait sets span 95 (Crohn disease) to 2,191 (height) universe genes".

Per-group genes with results: baseline 393 (7 timeouts), srv 290 (110 timeouts!), cpg 397 (3), topo 377 (23). Comparison bases vs baseline (n_common): srv 289, cpg 391, topo 371. Topology rerun timeout count = 23 (confirmed). Any cited "common genes" must be 289/391/371 for srv/cpg/topo; 393/290/397/377 are per-group result counts.

item5_tier4_correction.reported_p_values_convention: uncorrected raw Fisher/Spearman p (tier4_empirical_disjointness.csv has no q columns; phase9_tier4_disjointness.py applies no multiple-testing correction)
item5_tier4_correction.verdict: Both statements are numerically correct but the framing is contradictory. The CSV/JSON report raw P (Methods "reported uncorrected" is true of the reported values); the Results BH-across-six is an additional on-the-fly sensitivity, and it replicates exactly: Spearman q=4.5e-5 and caMPRA depletion q=8.1e-5 survive (q<0.02), GD hCONDEL depletion q=0.074 does not. Fix: Methods should say Tier-4 P values are reported uncorrected WITH a BH-across-six sensitivity stated in Results (or drop the Results BH). Note: tier4_empirical_disjointness.json subset_table/rate_difference still carry pre-hCONDEL-fix numbers (n=183) while the CSV is post-fix (n=112) - the JSON should be regenerated for consistency.
